title: "Flagged only by nrtqclib"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full

Observations nrtqclib flags bad and the input does not, over the same
profiles as [Flag differences in NRT](analyses-flags.qmd): at sea, marked
NRT, and not estimated to carry delayed mode flags, each variable over its
own profiles.

nrtqclib records which of its checks failed, so each of these can be traced
to the check, or checks, behind it. Set against which tests the producer
says it runs, a disagreement is either expected (the producer does not run
the test) or a sign that two versions of one test differ.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
table = app.analysisTable
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
variableLabel = (n) => meta.variables.find((v) => v.name === n)?.label ?? n
status = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_status") : null
nrtqclibOnly = new Map((status ?? [])
  .filter((r) => r.status === "nrtqclib_only")
  .map((r) => [`${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`, r.n_obs]))

// What each regional centre said about the test behind a check, from their
// answers (docs/REGIONAL_QC.md). The ids are those of config/test_nrt.yaml;
// a product not listed, such as a global one, gets "not described".
REGIONAL_RUNS = ({
  ar_ar: {
    global_range: "yes", regional_range: "yes", spike: "yes", gradient: "yes",
    stuck_value: "yes", density_inversion: "yes, at 0.05"
  },
  bo_bo: {
    global_range: "yes", regional_range: "yes", spike: "yes", gradient: "no",
    stuck_value: "no", density_inversion: "yes, at 0.05",
    pressure_increasing: "yes, on the whole profile"
  },
  mo_mo: {
    global_range: "yes", regional_range: "yes", spike: "yes", gradient: "yes",
    stuck_value: "yes", density_inversion: "not run yet"
  }
})
producerRuns = (datasetId, item) =>
  REGIONAL_RUNS[datasetId] ? (REGIONAL_RUNS[datasetId][item] ?? "not asked") : "not described"
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

## Which checks account for them

An observation can fail more than one check. The dark part of a bar is the
observations this check alone flagged, which nothing else in nrtqclib would
have caught; the light part is those it flagged together with other checks.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "items_attribution",
  "Observations only nrtqclib flags, as a share of all observations, by the check that failed. Checks that never contributed are left out. Note the different scales across products.",
  "Bar charts per product and variable of nrtqclib-only observations by check."
) : html``
```

The table gives, for one product, each check's failures, how many of them
the input flags too, and the share of the observations only nrtqclib flags
that the check accounts for. The last column is what the regional centre
said about the same test: "not asked" is a test it was not asked about and
did not mention, and the global products are "not described", since their
QC is not the regional centres'.

```{ojs}
byItem = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_by_item") : null
viewof itemDataset = meta && byItem
  ? Inputs.select([...new Set(byItem.map((r) => r.dataset_id))], { label: "Product", format: name })
  : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta && byItem ? table(
  byItem.filter((r) => r.dataset_id === itemDataset && r.n_fail > 0),
  [
    { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
    { key: "item", label: "Check", align: "left", format: (_, r) => app.qcCheck(r.column, meta.variables).label },
    { key: "n_fail", label: "Failed" },
    { key: "n_fail_agree_bad", label: "Input flags too", title: "Share of the check's failures the input flags bad as well", format: (v, r) => app.formatSmallShare(v, r.n_fail) },
    { key: "n_fail_nrtqclib_only", label: "Only nrtqclib" },
    { key: "share_of_only", label: "Of all nrtqclib only", title: "Share of the variable's observations only nrtqclib flags that this check failed", format: (_, r) => app.formatSmallShare(r.n_fail_nrtqclib_only, nrtqclibOnly.get(`${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`)) },
    { key: "n_alone_nrtqclib_only", label: "This check alone" },
    { key: "producer", label: "The producer runs it", align: "left", render: (_, r) => document.createTextNode(producerRuns(r.dataset_id, r.item)) }
  ]
) : html``
```

The commonest sets of failing checks behind the observations only nrtqclib
flags, over every NRT product together. A column is one set; the dots below
it say which checks are in it.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "items_combinations",
  "The ten commonest sets of failing nrtqclib checks among observations only nrtqclib flags, pooled over the NRT products.",
  "UpSet charts, one per variable, of check combinations."
) : html``
```

Placed the same way as on [Flagged only by the input](analyses-flags-original.qmd#where-they-sit-in-their-profiles):
against the observations nrtqclib calls good in the same profile, by
pressure.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "items_shape_nrtqclib",
  "Observations only nrtqclib flags, by where they sit in their profile against the observations nrtqclib calls good: all of the profile, a stretch above the shallowest good level, a stretch below the deepest, or between them, alone or with others. The number at the end of a bar is the observations it is made of.",

) : html``
```

## How one test can differ

Where both sides run a test, they can still disagree. The table below gives
nrtqclib's check as it is run here, and the ways another implementation of
the same test can differ. Some of these differences were measured on an
earlier implementation of the same tests, run on the Arctic products for
comparison; that implementation is not the input's QC, but it shows how
much each design choice moves the flags.

| Check | nrtqclib, as run here | How another implementation can differ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pressure increasing | Keeps the order the levels were recorded in, and fails a level whose pressure repeats the previous one or is shallower than any reached before it. | Sorting each profile by pressure before the tests hides a reversal, and dropping repeated pressures removes those levels instead of flagging them. The earlier implementation did both: on the Arctic products the levels it dropped matched the ones this check fails, so nothing of this kind was ever flagged. |
| Density inversion | Potential density (sigma-0) at each level; both levels of a consecutive pair fail when the lower one is lighter by more than 0.03 kg/m³. A level with no density breaks the comparison. | The Arctic and Baltic centres give 0.05 kg/m³ per dbar. In-situ density instead of potential density cancels part of an inversion by the pressure difference between the levels, the more so the further apart they are; comparing across missing levels adds pairs. The earlier implementation, with in-situ density and 0.05 kg/m³, agreed with this check on about a third of the levels either one flagged. |
| Temperature flag carried over | Raises the salinity flag wherever the temperature flag is 3 or 4, whatever test set it. | Flagging each variable on its own leaves salinity good beside a bad temperature. None of the regional centres mention carrying a flag over. |
| Stuck value | Fails a whole profile whose non-missing values are all the same, from 2 values up. | A larger minimum leaves short profiles unjudged: the earlier implementation needed more than 5 levels. |
| Spike and gradient | The level against its neighbours in recorded order. Spike fails above 6.0 °C or 0.9 in salinity above 500 dbar, and 2.0 °C or 0.3 below; gradient above 9.0 °C or 1.5, and 3.0 °C or 0.5. | The same formula and thresholds are common; taking the neighbours in pressure order, or after levels were dropped, changes which values are compared. The Baltic does not run the gradient test. |
| Regional range | One pair of ranges per region set, assigned per product. Temperature: -1.92 to 25 °C in the Arctic, -2.5 to 40 °C in the Baltic, 10 to 40 °C in the Mediterranean; salinity 2 to 40 in all three. | The region can be looked up per position from a grid, with bounds of its own: the earlier implementation's Arctic lower bound for temperature was -1.93 °C. |
| Global range | Temperature -2.5 to 40 °C, salinity 2 to 41. | Used only where a region has no bounds of its own, rather than on top of them. |
| Digit rollover | Fails a jump of more than 10 °C or 5 in salinity from the previous level. | Not mentioned by any regional centre. |

## Read together

- **Temperature flag carried over** accounts for most of the salinity only
  nrtqclib flags in every product, and nearly all of it outside the Baltic:
  nrtqclib passes a bad temperature on to salinity, the input does not. In
  the Arctic regional product most of it covers whole profiles, the
  salinity of profiles whose temperature is flagged bad throughout.
- **Pressure increasing** accounts for most of what only nrtqclib flags in
  the Arctic and Mediterranean global products, and the input flags little
  of what it fails, as a producer that sorts each profile by pressure
  would: it never sees a reversal.
- **Density inversion** accounts for most of the temperature only nrtqclib
  flags in the regional products. The Arctic and Baltic centres run it, with a larger threshold,
  and their input flags only a small share of nrtqclib's failures; the
  Mediterranean centre does not run it yet.
- **The Baltic's stuck value and gradient failures** are expected
  disagreements: the centre runs neither test. Its spike test does run, yet
  its input flags few of nrtqclib's spike failures, so the two spike tests
  must differ.
- **Regional range** in the Mediterranean global temperature: nrtqclib's
  lower bound for the Mediterranean is 10 °C, and the input flags about
  half of what it fails.
